subject: Data handback & escrow timelines — order form clarifications
messages:
From: Amal Shah <amal.shah@medtek.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medtek.com, compliance@medtek.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data handback / escrow window — Order Form Qs

Hi Jonas / Vanessa,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. A few compliance questions from our side before procurement will sign:

- For session payloads and inference inputs, we need confirmation that these are ephemeral by default and covered by a 90-day accessible retention window only.
- For billing logs and aggregated telemetry required for dispute resolution, what retention do you propose, and can we get assurances they are masked and stored in our KMS?
- We expect a defined escrow/handback procedure in the order form for legal holds. MedTek legal wants a 180-day escrow hold option that triggers on a preserved dataset export.
- Please confirm deletion timelines: soft-delete workflow, backup retention, and hard-delete / crypto-erase cadence.

Can you reply with the exact clause language you recommend so our legal/procurement teams can review? I attached a small retention matrix.

Thanks,
Amal
Amal Shah
Head of Compliance, MedTek Solutions

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Amal Shah <amal.shah@medtek.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data handback / escrow window — Order Form Qs

Hi Amal — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the suggested order-form language and operational notes (attached: order_form_v3.pdf). Summary of the proposed terms below:

- Residency / retention windows (default):
  * Session payloads & transient request data: ephemeral, 90 days accessible, then soft-deleted.
  * Billing/usage logs (masked): retained 365 days for reconciliation and dispute resolution; encrypted with customer KMS keys; can be set shorter by request.
  * Backups & disaster-recovery snapshots: retained 365 days but marked for scheduled purge; backups subject to the same KMS encryption and deletion workflow.

- Deletion pipeline:
  * Soft-delete window: 30 calendar days after a deletion request or contract termination (data remains logically inaccessible).
  * Hard-delete / crypto-erase: initiated 14 calendar days after soft-delete expiry; complete crypto-erase confirmed by audit entry.
  * For backups, purge initiated within 30 days of hard-delete; full removal may take up to 90 days depending on underlying storage replication, with an audit trail.

- Escrow / handback:
  * Escrow hold (optional): 180 calendar days by default when triggered for legal hold; can be extended to 210 days on request (see section 7.2 redlines).
  * Export / handback process: we provide a secure export (SFTP or pre-signed, customer KMS-wrapped archive) and a checklist for verification.
  * Proof of deletion: we provide a signed certificate with hash manifests and audit log extract when deletion completes.

Operational notes: we support HSM-backed KMS, audit logs retained 2 years by default (can be extended). We also include an SLA for execution timelines in the order form.

If this aligns, Vanessa can confirm the operational runbook items (handoff windows, verification steps) and we can produce a redline for DocuSign.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data handback / escrow window — Order Form Qs

Hi Amal — quick operational follow-up with timelines so your ops/legal teams can plan: 

- Export & verification: once escrow is triggered, we will provision an export job within 24 hours and provide a pre-signed, KMS-wrapped tarball for download. Customer has 5 business days to verify the export; we retain the copy in escrow for the agreed hold period (180/210 days).
- Execution SLAs: full data handback (all customer files, manifests, and verification report) — target within 5 business days of request; certificate-of-deletion for remaining storage objects — within 30 calendar days post-handback.
- Backups & replication caveat: restoration-dependent backups may require up to 90 calendar days to be fully scrubbed from all replicas; we provide hashed proof and a deletion timeline report.
- Auditability: you will receive an audit extract (including operation IDs) and a signed statement of crypto-erase when hard-delete completes.

I attached the operational runbook and a retention matrix screenshot to show the mapping between data classes, retention windows, and the purge pipeline (escrow_procedure.docx; screenshot-retention-matrix.png).

If you want the escrow hold to be 210 days instead of 180, we can accept that with a small amendment to clause 7.2 — happy to add that redline for procurement.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Lead, Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
